cards.title: Opening
cards.applicability: How should the campaign start? Read when choosing initial expansion, commanders, scouting and construction before an operation is settled.

cards.title: Global strategy
cards.applicability: Which course and measurable stages lead to victory fastest? Read when choosing or revising the course, assessing readiness or reviewing stalled conquest.

cards.title: Development
cards.applicability: How can income, production, recruitment or delivery unlock the next operation? Read when choosing economic expansion or resolving a resource or reinforcement bottleneck.

cards.title: Offensive operation
cards.applicability: Which conquest or breakthrough and follow-up should come next? Read before choosing an offensive operation and after passage opening, capture, substantial losses or reinforcement; compare actors and base exposure.

cards.title: Main army idle
cards.applicability: Why is the main army making no useful progress, and what can unblock it? Read when movement remains unused, routes or goals are blocked, or execution misses a deadline.

cards.title: Recovery
cards.applicability: How should lost combat readiness be restored? Read after army or commander loss, retreat/surrender, or when low mana may justify recovery before battle.

cards.title: Defense
cards.applicability: How can a threatened base be protected? Read when threats or protection change, including before recall, departure, troop transfers or opening enemy access.

cards.title: Town after capture
cards.applicability: How should a captured town be used, and when can the army leave? Read after capture or when choosing departure, extending a hold or trading bases.

cards.title: Exploration
cards.applicability: How can missing town access be opened? Read for blocked conquest/expansion, targets on another level, key/border/passage prerequisites, scouting or collector assignments, and helper replacement after confirmed loss.

cards.title: Finish the game
cards.applicability: How can the advantage become a confirmed victory? Read when comparing a decisive attack with minor targets or waiting, planning elimination, or returning a town before public townless loss.
